title: Add RAG session recorder demo + docs for local replay and debugging
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: New quickstart: RAG session recorder for local replay and deterministic debugging. Includes demo app, Docker compose, docs and tests.
description:
Motivation: debugging RAG flows with tool-calling and adapters is hard because reproducing the exact sequence of model outputs, tool calls, and vector DB lookups is non-trivial. This quickstart introduces a lightweight 'session recorder' that captures full request/response traces (prompts, model outputs, tool calls, KV/cache events, and retrieval hits) and a local replay harness that deterministically replays sessions against a pinned model or a mocked runtime.

What this PR adds (single continuous description):
- session-recorder/README.md: developer quickstart that explains recorder architecture, replay modes (deterministic vs. stochastic), and privacy knobs.
- session-recorder/demo/: small Node/TS demo application that runs a RAG pipeline wired to the recorder. Shows tool-calling to a simple facts service and a mocked vector DB.
- session-recorder/docker-compose.yml: runs the demo + recorder + replay web UI locally for easier onboarding.
- session-recorder/.env.example: runtime switches (RECORD=true, REDWOOD_API_KEY=..., REPLAY_MODE=deterministic).
- session-recorder/test/playback.spec.ts: integration test that records a short session, replays it, and asserts identical event sequence and deterministic outputs when REPLAY_MODE=deterministic and model seed is pinned.
- docs/session-recorder.md: integrated docs for the docs site (how to install, security notes, retention policy and suggested evals).
- assets/session-recorder-diagram.svg: architecture diagram for the README and docs.

Checklist: [x] Demo runs locally via docker-compose [x] Unit/integration tests added [x] Docs and diagram included [x] Telemetry hooks instrumented but opt-in by default

How to try locally (short):
1) cp session-recorder/.env.example .env && fill REDWOOD_API_KEY and set RECORD=true
2) docker-compose up --build
3) Open http://localhost:8080 to start a demo conversation and then press "Record session"
4) Use the replay UI to load recorded session and choose "deterministic replay" to validate behavior

Security & privacy: recordings can include PII. Recorder defaults to redaction of fields matching a small patterns whitelist (emails, credit-card-like numbers) and exposes an opt-in retention TTL. The docs section shows how to plug in a KMS-backed encrypt-on-disk adapter before enabling long-term storage.

Motivation and scope notes: This quickstart is intentionally opinionated: it favors a developer ergonomics-first path (local run, Docker, deterministic replay) rather than a production-grade archival pipeline. It is meant as a developer tool to reproduce bugs, create ground-truth prompt/response pairs for regression tests, and to help SREs triage incidents involving tool-calling and retrieval mismatches.

Related: Linear ENG-8721 (session replay prototype), PM-342 (developer debugging UX), Support SUP-1124 (customer reproducer request).

review_conversation: Diego Morales (reviewer): Nice ergonomics. A couple of nits: can we avoid using REDWOOD_API_KEY in .env.example and prefer a local-token file for the demo? Also the docker-compose exposes the recorder port on 0.0.0.0: consider limiting to 127.0.0.1 for safety.

Asha Patel (author): Good call — switched the example to use LOCAL_TOKEN_FILE and updated README. Docker compose now binds recorder to 127.0.0.1. Added note in docs about network exposure and experimental nature.
Katrina Liu (reviewer): Integration test is great. One request: add an explicit assertion that tool-call timing metadata is present, we've had bugs where timing gets dropped in the pipeline.
Asha Patel (author): Added timing assertion in playback.spec.ts and a small test fixture that simulates delayed tool responses to validate KV cache and timing capture.
Evan Brooks (approver): Verified demo runs locally, e2e passed in my run. Approving — small docs wording tweak suggested (see inline).
Katrina Liu (approver): Approved after timing assertion change.

merge_commit_message: Add RAG session recorder quickstart: demo, replay harness, docs
notes: This quickstart is safe to land: all telemetry is opt-in and env examples default to RECORD=false. We should follow up with a short blog post and add a reference from the debugging section of the docs site.
testing_instructions: Run tests: cd redwood-quickstarts/session-recorder && npm ci && npm test. To run e2e: docker-compose up --build then run npm run test:e2e. The integration test requires Docker to be available.
changelog_summary: Developer quickstart: session recorder for deterministic RAG replay and debugging. Includes demo app, docker-compose, tests and docs. Opt-in telemetry; security guidance included.
